newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes down at $17.77 as bears keep hold.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes down at $17.77 as bears keep hold.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed towards the lower end of the day's trading range on Wednesday as sellers inspired by steadily weakening spreads kept the upper hand, brokers said.
Front month August last traded at $17.77, 31 cents down from Tuesday and nine cents off the low of $17.68. September finished at $17.88, down 33 cents.
"There's been a bit of buying on the way down but spreads have looked weaker steadily all day and what we've seen now is just a continuation of this morning's fall," one broker said.
The bearish tone was unaffected by a tough statement criticising Iraq by the U.N. commission dismantling Iraq's weapons of mass destruction.
Wall Street funds are still short ahead of next week's OPEC meeting but any move substantially above $18 before then could test nerves among the shorts.
"Longer term I still see it weaker. But I think just at the moment if I was a short I'd be nervous," said another broker.
Support for August Brent is seen around $17.70 followed by $17.40, with resistance at around $17.90.
NYMEX, July WTI was 41 cents adrift at $18.82 a barrel.
Earlier IPE gas oil closed down $5 at the lows on steady technical selling inspired by bearish API figures. The front month July settled at $158.75 a tonne.
Brokers said EIA weekly stocks figures mostly confirmed American Petroleum Institute data showing a build in gasoline stocks and a decline in crude stocks.

The API figures also showed U.S. crude oil imports for the week ended June 13 hit a record 9.4 million barrels per day (bpd), up nearly a million barrels per day. At the same time, gasoline output set a record 8.23 million bpd after breaking the record set two weeks prior.
